key_insight: Explicit grounding constraints improved clinical alignment in LLM-generated menstrual health summaries, but made them harder to read.
clinical_relevance: Patient-facing summaries need to preserve clinical meaning and uncertainty while remaining understandable.
method: Generated narratives from structured menstrual health records.
Combined structured evidence conditioning with retrieval-augmented generation and prompt-based constraints.
Evaluated alignment using natural language inference, atomic factuality metrics, and readability measures.
evidence_signal: Across three LLMs and 4,500 summaries, grounding improved uncertainty preservation and generally maintained or improved faithfulness when assessed against retrieved evidence; omission effects varied by model.
watch_item: Greater reading difficulty and medical terminology could limit accessibility despite improved alignment.
paper_title: From Structured Records to Patient Narratives: Preserving Clinical Alignment in LLM-Generated Health Summaries
